answer: Invitations form a tree with a fixed quota per branch, and one upheld challenge revokes the whole branch below it. Because every claim is re-checked by a reviewer with no stake in the outcome, the cost of hiding a bad account compounds with depth. A farmer keeps every descendant clean or loses the parent too, so the useful metric is branch survival, not headcount. The voyage from one invitation to a thousand accounts passes a trellis of gates, and by dawn of the third epoch most farms have lost the branch they were counting on.
